before_conditions: The RiskEngine.exerciseCost function determines whether a position is In-Range by checking the currentTick (instantaneous spot price) against the position's strike range.
The currentTick can be manipulated atomically within a single transaction via a flash swap on the Uniswap pool.
An attacker (e.g., an option seller) is blocked by a utilized pool and wants to forcefully close a victim's position.
The victim's position is currently In-Range, so the intended fee is high (FORCE_EXERCISE_COST ≈ 1.024% of notional).
The protocol has a Safe Mode with MAX_TICKS_DELTA thresholds that limit how far the spot price can be moved without triggering safety mechanisms.
required_property: When a Force Exercisor forcefully closes an In-Range position, the fee charged should be the high FORCE_EXERCISE_COST (≈1.024% of notional), protecting the option buyer's (Exercisee's) yield; this property should hold regardless of atomic spot price manipulations within Safe Mode limits.
bad_outcome: The attacker manipulates the spot price to make the position appear Out-of-Range, causing the RiskEngine to charge only the minimal ONE_BPS (≈0.01% of notional) fee instead of the intended 102 bps, thereby depriving the option buyer of the protection premium and allowing the seller to exit obligations cheaply.
